questions.question: Which of these conditions enhance the potential of MFIS to attract more resources and expand services to their clients ?

options.text: Financially viable and self - sustaining MFIs
Ability to disintegrate from communities they operate in
Ability to lend large amounts of loans

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Financially viable and self - sustaining MFIs.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Financial viability** and self-sustainability are crucial for MFIs (Microfinance Institutions) to grow and serve more clients effectively.
 
• Being **financially viable** allows MFIs to attract more resources, including investments and loans, which can be used to expand their services.
 
• MFIs that are self-sustaining can **reinvest their profits** into the business, enhancing their capacity to provide more and larger loans to clients.
 
• A focus on financial sustainability helps MFIs to reduce their dependence on external funding, such as **foreign aid**, making them more robust against financial crises.

questions.question: How many countries are part of SAARC?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**8**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) **was founded on **December 8, 1985**.
 
• Its Secretariat was established in **Kathmandu, Nepal,** on January 17, 1987.
 
• SAARC comprises eight member countries:** Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka.**
 
• The objectives of SAARC include enhancing the welfare of the people of South Asia, improving their standard of living, fostering economic growth, social advancement, and cultural enrichment in the region.
 
• SAARC also aims to ensure every individual has the opportunity to lead a dignified life and realize their full potential.
 
• Additionally, SAARC endeavours to strengthen collaboration with other developing nations and to engage with international and regional organizations sharing similar goals and objectives.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• SAARC **Heads of State convene** at annual Summits, with the most recent one held in Kathmandu in 2014.
 
• Subsequently, Nepal has been hosting informal meetings of SAARC Foreign Ministers annually. The latest such gathering took place virtually in September 2020 alongside the UNGA.
 
• To address the challenges posed by the COVID-19 pandemic, SAARC devised and enacted a regional emergency fund totaling approximately 22 million USD.
 
• This fund aims to enhance cooperation among member states in combatting the pandemic's effects and supporting collective efforts towards recovery and resilience.

questions.question: Chaitrual and Phulaich are the festivals of which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Himachal Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chaitrual and Phulaich** are the festivals of **Himachal Pradesh**.
 
• Chaitrual is a widely celebrated festival in the Sirmaur area, occurring during the Chaitra month's bright fortnight on a specific day.
 
• During this occasion, households clear and adorn their walls, painting them and embellishing them with depictions of male animals and crops, symbolizing abundance.
 
• It is also referred to as the **"festival of pictures."**
 
• In the Kinnaur district of Himachal Pradesh, the Phulaich Festival, alternatively known as Ookayand Festival or Ukyam Festival, is observed in September.
 
• The term 'Oo' denotes 'flowers,' while 'Kayang' signifies 'festival,' making Phulaich synonymous with the** 'festival of flowers.'**
 
• On the 16th day of the Hindu month of 'Bhadrapada,' ten Rajputs from the village venture to the high hills to gather select flowers from the blooming season of wildflowers in the upper regions of Kinnaur district.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Himachal Pradesh **is a state located in the northern region of India.
 
• Nestled in the Western Himalayas, Himachal Pradesh is one of the thirteen mountain states and boasts a rugged landscape marked by numerous peaks and extensive river systems.
 
• As the northernmost state in India, it shares borders with the union territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh to the north.
 
• To the west lie the states of Punjab, while Haryana borders it to the southwest and Uttarakhand to the southeast.
 
• Additionally, Himachal Pradesh has a narrow boundary with Uttar Pradesh to the south. Towards the east, the state shares an international border with the Tibet Autonomous Region in China.

questions.question: Which of the following erstwhile Princely states was primarily associated with Kathak ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Avadh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Princely state Avadh** was primarily associated with **Kathak**.
 
• **The National Institute of Kathak Dance**, commonly known as Kathak Kendra, is the foremost institution dedicated to the classical dance form of Kathak.
 
• As a unit of the Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's National Academy of Music, Dance, and Drama, it is located in New Delhi.
 
• Established in 1964, Kathak Kendra primarily focuses on Kathak training but also offers courses in Hindustani classical music (vocal) and Pakhawaj and Tabla. With the decline of royal patronage after India gained independence in 1947, Kathak exponents and gurus faced challenges. Many began teaching privately.
 
• Under the patronage of the Awadh state, Lachhu Maharaj relocated to Bombay, while his brother, Shambhu Maharaj, along with his nephew, moved to Delhi in 1955.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shambhu Maharaj **was honored with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship, the highest award bestowed by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, in 1967.
 
• Following Shambhu Maharaj's passing in 1970, his nephew, Birju Maharaj, a renowned Kathak dancer and guru, assumed leadership roles at the institution.
 
• Birju Maharaj's tenure witnessed a transformation in Kathak performance, adapting it from intimate gatherings to large-scale productions in modern theaters.
 
• He introduced several acclaimed ballets during this period, gradually transitioning Kathak from a solo dance form to one that embraced group performances.

questions.question:
Identify the INCORRECT statement/s concerning SHGs.

i. They include voluntary groups of up to 20 socially and economically homogenous people.

ii. There is no need to follow the well-defined rules and bye - laws for SHGs.

iii. In April 1996, RBI declared SHG - BLP as a priority sector lending activity.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only ii**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Self-help Groups (SHGs) **are informal associations formed by people with similar economic and social backgrounds to collectively address their challenges and enhance their quality of life.
 
• These groups are typically self-managed and operated by their members. Individuals often come together with the assistance of non-governmental organizations (NGOs) or government agencies to address common issues and uplift their living standards.
 
• The roots of SHGs in India can be traced back to the establishment of the Self-Employed Women’s Association (SEWA) in 1972.
 
• Even earlier instances of self-organization existed, such as the formation of the women’s wing of the Textile Labour Association (TLA) of Ahmedabad in 1954, aimed at training women from mill worker families in various skills.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] 

**Important Points__**

 
• To foster the growth of the SHG movement, the government should create an enabling environment and act as a facilitator and promoter. Additionally, expanding the SHG movement to credit-deficient areas like Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, and the North-Eastern states is crucial for broader socioeconomic development.
 
• To bolster financial infrastructure, including that of the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD), it's imperative to embrace extensive IT-enabled communication and capacity-building initiatives in these states.
 
• This approach can enhance accessibility and efficiency in financial services delivery, particularly in rural and remote areas.

questions.question: Use of more labour and capital inputs on the given land under cultivation is referred to as ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**intensive cultivation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Use of more labour and capital inputs on the given land under cultivation is referred to as** ****intensive cultivation**.
 
• **Intensive agriculture, **also referred to as intensive farming, conventional agriculture, or industrial agriculture, is characterized by the significant utilization of labor and capital in relation to land area.
 
• It involves higher levels of input and output per unit of agricultural land area compared to extensive farming practices.
 
• In contrast, extensive farming involves cultivating large farms with relatively smaller inputs, such as cash and labor, and is typically practiced in regions with extensive land and sparse population.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Extensive farming,** also known as extensive agriculture, is characterized by the use of minimal inputs of labor, fertilizers, and capital in relation to the land area being farmed. 
 
• **Hybrid cultivation **involves the cross-breeding of two different varieties of plants to combine desired traits. 
 
• **In a Capitalistic farming system,** farming activities are directed and managed by individual entrepreneurs who exercise control over the agricultural processes.

questions.question: When was Kapil Dev awarded with Padma Shri Award?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1982**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kapil Dev,** an iconic figure in Indian cricket, was honored with the** Padma Shri in 1982** and the **Padma Bhushan in 1991**, two of** India's highest civilian awards**. 
 
• He was named the Indian Cricketer of the Century in 2002 and inducted into the International Cricket Council's Hall of Fame in 2010, recognizing his exceptional contributions to the sport. 
 
• Kapil Dev Nikhanj, an esteemed former Indian cricketer, is renowned as one of the finest all-rounders in cricket history, excelling as a fast-medium bowler and a powerful middle-order batsman.
 
• He holds the unique distinction of being the only player to have amassed over 400 wickets (434 wickets) and scored more than 5,000 runs in Test matches.
 
• As captain, Dev led the Indian cricket team to victory in the 1983 Cricket World Cup, making history as the first Indian captain to achieve this milestone. Notably, he remains the youngest captain, having achieved this feat at the age of 24.
 
• Retiring in 1994, he was the first player to claim 200 wickets in One Day Internationals (ODIs) and held the world record for the highest number of wickets in Test cricket until it was surpassed by Courtney Walsh in 2000.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Padma Shri **stands as the fourth-highest civilian award in India, following the Bharat Ratna, the Padma Vibhushan, and the Padma Bhushan. 
 
• Established on January 2, 1954, this accolade is bestowed in acknowledgment of outstanding contributions across a wide array of fields such as arts, education, industry, literature, science, acting, medicine, social service, and public affairs. 
 
• Annually conferred by the Government of India, it is a prestigious honor awarded on India's Republic Day.

questions.question: What is the most generally used indicator of overall economic performance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Per capita Gross National Product**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Per capita Gross National Product** is the most generally used indicator of **overall economic performance**.
 
• Per capita Gross National Product (GNP) is indeed a widely used indicator to gauge the economic performance of a country.
 
• It measures the average economic output per person in a given country, providing insight into the standard of living and economic well-being of its citizens.
 
• By dividing the total GNP of a country by its population, policymakers, economists, and analysts can assess trends in economic growth, compare the economic performance of different countries, and make informed decisions regarding economic policies and strategies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Human Development Index (HDI)** indeed serves as a comprehensive measure of a country's social and economic development, encompassing key factors like education, health, and income. By combining indicators such as mean years of schooling, expected years of schooling, life expectancy at birth, and gross national income (GNI) per capita, the HDI provides a holistic assessment of human well-being and development across different nations.
 
• **The Physical Quality of Life Index (PQLI)** offers another perspective on societal well-being by considering various social factors, including life expectancy, infant mortality rate, and literacy rate. It provides a broader understanding of the overall quality of life within a population, highlighting areas for improvement and policy intervention.
 
• **The standard of living** refers to the overall level of prosperity and well-being enjoyed by individuals or communities, typically measured by factors such as income, access to basic needs, and quality of life indicators. It provides insight into the material comforts, services, and opportunities available to people within a given society or location, reflecting their economic and social status.

questions.question: The analysis of the interrelationship between the economy and the environment in the economic environmental accounting system was put forward by ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**United Nations Statistical Office**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The analysis of the interrelationship between **the economy and the environment in the economic environmental accounting system** was put forward by** ****United Nations Statistical Office**.
 
• The System of Environmental-Economic Accounting (SEEA), endorsed by the United Nations Statistical Commission in 2012, serves as the official international framework for natural capital accounting.
 
• It offers a standardized approach to organizing and presenting statistics concerning the environment and its interconnectedness with the economy.
 
• At its core, SEEA comprises two key components: the Central Framework (SEEA-CF) and Ecosystems Accounting (SEEA-EA).
 
• The SEEA-CF adopts an economic perspective, analyzing how natural resources such as fish, timber, and water are utilized in production and consumption processes.
 
• Additionally, it examines the resultant pollution, encompassing waste, water, and air emissions. On the other hand, SEEA-EA complements the Central Framework by focusing on ecosystems and their significance in enhancing human well-being through the provision of identifiable ecosystem services.
 
• This component offers insights into the contribution of ecosystems to various aspects of human life, offering a holistic understanding of environmental sustainability and economic development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The United Nations Statistics Division (UNSD) **is dedicated to advancing the global statistical system, facilitating the harmonization of statistical practices and standards worldwide.
 
• **The Central Statistics Office (CSO)** is a governmental agency in India operating under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation. Its primary responsibilities include coordinating statistical activities across India and developing and upholding statistical standards.
 
• **The National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (NEERI)** in Nagpur, originally established in 1958 as the Central Public Health Engineering Research Institute (CPHERI), focuses on research and development in the field of environmental engineering.
 
• **DES** serves as the Principal Statistical Organisation of the State Government, overseeing all statistical activities within the state. It is designated as the "Nodal Agency" responsible for coordinating statistical endeavors throughout the state.

questions.question: Who among the following was the disciple of Ramakrishna Paramahansa?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Swami Vivekananda**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Narendranath Dutta, renowned as Swami Vivekananda,** emerged as one of the most prominent disciples of** Ramakrishna Paramahansa**.
 
• Born in 1863, Swami Vivekananda propagated the belief that all religions emphasize the unity of God and the equality of humanity.
 
• Following Ramakrishna's passing, Swami Vivekananda played a pivotal role in popularizing his teachings and establishing both the Ramakrishna Order and the Ramakrishna Mission.
 
• The Ramakrishna Order offers spiritual guidance to both householders and monastics, while the Ramakrishna Mission is dedicated to charitable endeavors, education, and social welfare.
 
• Functioning as a non-profit organization, the Ramakrishna Mission aims to facilitate individuals in their quest for spiritual enlightenment and salvation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Dayanand Saraswati **was an eminent Indian philosopher, social reformer, and the founder of the Arya Samaj, a movement aimed at revitalizing Hinduism. His seminal work, "Satyarth Prakash," remains a cornerstone text, offering profound insights into Vedic philosophy and elucidating various human duties and concepts.
 
• **Swami Sahajananda,** a notable Indian politician, served as a Member of the Legislative Assembly of Tamil Nadu. He represented the Chidambaram constituency as an Indian National Congress candidate in both the 1952 and 1957 elections, contributing significantly to the state's legislative proceedings.
 
• **Swami Shraddhanand, **also known as Mahatma Munshi Ram Vij, was a revered Arya Samaj sannyasi and a prominent figure in India's struggle for independence. He dedicated his life to promoting the teachings of Dayanand Saraswati and played a pivotal role in advocating social reform and national awakening.

questions.question: Which National Waterway runs from Haldia to Prayagraj?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**National Waterway 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **National Waterway 1** runs from **Haldia to Prayagraj**.
 
• The National Waterway 1 (NW-1), also known as the Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly river system, spans from Prayagraj in Uttar Pradesh to Haldia in West Bengal, traversing through Patna and Bhagalpur in Bihar along the Ganges river.
 
• Stretching over 1,620 km (1,010 mi), NW-1 holds the distinction of being India's longest waterway.
 
• Renowned for its strategic location, NW-1 passes through several states including West Bengal, Jharkhand, Bihar, and Uttar Pradesh, connecting major cities
 
• Designated as a national waterway in October 1986, NW-1 facilitates navigation by mechanical boats up to Patna, playing a pivotal role in inland water transportation in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **National Waterway 2 (NW-2)** is a segment of the Brahmaputra River stretching over 891 kilometers. It extends from the Bangladesh border near Dhubri to Sadiya in Assam. Officially designated as NW-2 on September 1, 1988, this waterway plays a crucial role in inland navigation in the northeastern region of India.
 
• **National Waterway 3 (NW-3) **spans 205 kilometers and serves as an inland navigational route in Kerala, India. Running from Kollam to Kottapuram, NW-3 was declared a National Waterway in 1993, facilitating transportation and trade within the state of Kerala.
 
• **National Waterway 4 (NW-4)** covers a distance of 1,095 kilometers, linking the Indian states of Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, and the union territory of Puducherry. This waterway connects the Krishna and Godavari rivers, serving as a vital transportation route for cargo and passenger movement in the region.

questions.question: Which of the following components is NOT related to the New India Literacy Programme?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Business and Enhancing skill Development**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Business and Enhancing skill Development component **is NOT related to the** New India Literacy Programme**.
 
• The government has initiated the **"New India Literacy Programme" (NILP)**, a Centrally Sponsored Scheme, set to run over five years from FYs 2022-23 to 2026-27.
 
• With a total financial outlay of Rs. 1037.90 crore, comprising a Central share of Rs. 700.00 crore and a State share of Rs. 337.90 crore, the scheme aims to target 5.00 crore non-literates aged 15 years and above.
 
• **NILP comprises five key components: Foundational Literacy and Numeracy, Critical Life Skills, Vocational Skills Development, Basic Education, and Continuing Education.**
 
• Beneficiaries are identified through door-to-door surveys conducted via a Mobile App by designated surveyors in the States/UTs.
 
• Alternatively, non-literates can register directly from any location via the mobile app to avail scheme benefits. Notably, the scheme hinges on volunteerism for teaching and learning, with volunteers able to register through the mobile app for this purpose.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The scheme is primarily technology-driven and relies heavily on online platforms for implementation. 
 
• Teaching and learning materials and resources are accessible through the DIKSHA platform of NCERT via mobile apps. 
 
• Additionally, alternative dissemination modes such as television, radio, and Samajik Chetna Kendra are also employed to spread Foundational Literacy and Numeracy. 
 
• The scheme is inclusive, targeting all non-literates aged 15 years and above, ensuring widespread access to its benefits.

questions.question: Which of the following rivers originates near Sihawa in Raipur district of Chhattisgarh, flows through Odisha, and eventually empties into the Bay of Bengal ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahanadi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Mahanadi River **begins its journey near **Sihawa in the Raipur district of Chhattisgarh**, then courses through Odisha before eventually reaching the Bay of Bengal.
 
• Regarded as one of the major east-flowing peninsular rivers in India, the Mahanadi holds significant importance, particularly in the state of Chhattisgarh.
 
• Stretching approximately 851 kilometers in length, it originates from the Shrungi mountains in Sihawa Tehsil of Dhamtari district.
 
• The river is also known by various names such as Kanaknandini, Chitrapalal, and Mahasweta.
 
• Prior to the construction of the Hirakud Dam, the Mahanadi River was navigable from its mouth all the way up to Arrang, situated approximately 250 kilometers from its source.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Krishna River, **coursing through the Deccan plateau, ranks as India's third-longest river, trailing only the Ganges and Godavari. It stands as the fourth-largest river in terms of both water inflows and river basin area in the country, following the Ganges, Indus, and Godavari.
 
• **The Godavari River, **stretching 1,465 kilometers, claims the title of India's second-longest river, surpassed only by the Ganga. It boasts the largest Peninsular river system and drains the third largest basin in India, encompassing approximately 10% of the nation's total geographical area.
 
• **The Kaveri**, also recognized as the** Cauvery** or its anglicized name, emerges as one of India's major rivers, traversing through the states of Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.

questions.question: Which of the following programmes of the Government of India aims to provide connectivity to unconnected habitations as part of a poverty reduction strategy ?

options.text: Prime Minister Rural Development Fellows Scheme

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY),** initiated by the Government of India, aims to enhance connectivity to previously unlinked habitations as a **key component of poverty alleviation efforts**.
 
• The government endeavors to establish rigorous technical and managerial standards while facilitating policy development and planning at the state level to ensure the sustainable management of rural road networks.
 
• As per the latest data provided by state governments through a survey conducted to identify the Core Network under the PMGSY program, approximately 1.67 lakh unconnected habitations are deemed eligible for inclusion in the program.
 
• This entails the construction of around 3.71 lakh kilometers of new roads for connectivity purposes and the upgrading of 3.68 lakh kilometers of existing roads.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Prime Minister's Rural Development Fellows (PMRDF) scheme **is a collaborative initiative between the Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD) and state governments aimed at diminishing poverty and enhancing the quality of life for individuals residing in rural India.
 
• **The Swarnjayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY)** is a governmental scheme established by the Ministry of Rural Development in April 1999 with the objective of assisting economically disadvantaged families in rural areas to achieve self-employment.
 
• **The National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM) **is a comprehensive poverty alleviation program implemented in India, focusing on empowering rural communities and fostering sustainable livelihoods.

questions.question: Who is credited with creating the popular Raga Miya Ki Malhar ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tansen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Miyan Tansen,** a distinguished classical music composer, musician, and vocalist, is credited with creating the popular raga Miyan Ki Malhar during the 16th century.
 
• He held a prominent position in the court of the Mughal Emperor Akbar and was revered as the **"Sangeet Samrat" or the "Monarch of Indian Music".**
 
• Miyan Ki Malhar, a monsoon raga, is often employed to herald the arrival of the monsoon season and to invoke rainfall.
 
• The melodic patterns of this raga have the ability to emulate the rumbling thunder of clouds and the cascading torrents of rain.
 
• Malhar, an ancient raga in Indian classical music, is deeply associated with the onset of torrential rains and is renowned for its evocative portrayal of the monsoon season.

**Important Points__**

Revered as an iconic figure in the cultural heritage of South Asia, he was renowned for his mysticism and spiritual devotion as a disciple of Nizamuddin Auliya of Delhi, India.

He is the eldest son of the legendary tabla player Alla Rakha and is widely regarded as one of the greatest tabla players in history.

questions.question: Name a unit designed for wet and dry bulb thermometers to protect temperature sensors from being affected by direct or reflected sunlight.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Stevenson screen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A Stevenson screen **serves as a protective shelter for meteorological instruments, such as **wet and dry bulb thermometers,** safeguarding them from direct sunlight and precipitation while facilitating free airflow.
 
• These screens are typically constructed from wood and painted white to reflect solar radiation effectively.
 
• Featuring louvered sides, Stevenson screens enable unrestricted air circulation around the thermometers, ensuring accurate temperature measurements.
 
• Moreover, they are strategically positioned 1.25 meters above the ground to minimize the influence of strong temperature gradients present at ground level.
 
• Thomas Stevenson, a notable Scottish civil engineer, credited with the design of the Stevenson screen in 1864. He is also recognized as the father of the renowned writer Robert Louis Stevenson.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Thomas Stevenson **was a pioneering Scottish civil engineer, renowned for his contributions to lighthouse design and meteorology. He designed over thirty lighthouses in and around Scotland, as well as the Stevenson screen used in meteorology.
 
• His innovative designs revolutionized lighthouse construction and set a new standard in the field.
 
• Stevenson held prestigious positions throughout his career, including serving as president of the Royal Scottish Society of Arts from 1859 to 1860 and as president of the Royal Society of Edinburgh from 1884 to 1886.
 
• Additionally, he played a key role as a co-founder of the Scottish Meteorological Society.

questions.question: Which article of the Indian Constitution deals with the formation of New States and Alteration of Areas, Boundaries or names of existing States ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 3 of the Indian Constitution **outlines the process for the formation of new States and the alteration of areas, boundaries, or names of existing States.
 
• In this regard, the **Parliament **may enact laws to:
 
 
• Form a new State by separation of territory from any State or by uniting two or more States or parts of States or by uniting any territory to a part of any State.
 
• Increase the area of any State.
 
• Diminish the area of any State.
 
• Alter the boundaries of any State.
 
• Alter the name of any State. 
 
 
 
• These provisions empower the Parliament to undertake significant changes in the territorial structure and nomenclature of States within the Indian Union.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Article 4 of the Constitution of India **enables changes to be made to the names of states in the Union of India and the allocation of seats each state receives in the Rajya Sabha. Additionally, it addresses incidental, supplemental, and consequential matters related to these changes.
 
• **Article 5 of the Constitution of India**, 1950, addresses citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution.
 
• **Article 6 of the Constitution **deals with the citizenship status of individuals who migrated from Pakistan to India during the partition between India and Pakistan.

questions.question: Ranjumoni Saikia was awarded the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award 2019 for her contribution to which classical dance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sattriya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ranjumoni Saikia** was awarded the **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award 2019** for her contribution to Sattriya.
 
• Among the **168 winners** from Assam were **Sattriya dancer Ranjumoni Saikia**, actor Pranjal Saikia, director Abinash Sharma, theatre artist Gunindra Nath Ojha, and folk artist Prashanna Gogoi.
 
• Sattriya dancer Ranjumoni Saikia, actor Pranjal Saikia, and director Abinash Sharma were specifically recognized as the recipients of the prize in 2019.
 
• Sattriya Nritya, commonly referred to as Sattriya, is a classical Indian dance form with roots dating back over 500 years in Assam.
 
• It holds a distinguished status as one of the eight principal classical dance styles of India.
 
• Introduced in the 15th century by Mahapurusha Sankaradeva, a revered Vaishnava saint and reformer from Assam, Sattriya was initially conceived as an integral component of Bhaona.
 
• Bhaona encompasses performances of one-act plays known as Ankiya Nat. Sattriya serves as a potent medium for propagating the Vaishnava faith, embodying spiritual themes and expressions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Sangeet Natak Akademi Award, **also known as the Akademi Puraskar, is a prestigious honor bestowed by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's National Academy of Music, Dance & Drama.
 
• Regarded as the highest recognition in the Indian performing arts realm, this award acknowledges individuals for their outstanding contributions.
 
• Initially instituted in 2003, the award comprised a cash prize of Rs. 50,000, along with a citation, an angavastram (a shawl), and a tamrapatra (a brass plaque).
 
• However, since 2009, the cash prize has been enhanced to ₹1,00,000.
 
• These accolades are conferred across various categories including music, dance, theatre, other traditional arts and puppetry, as well as for noteworthy contributions or scholarship in the field of performing arts.

questions.question: Name the transuranium element with atomic number 106, created by bombarding californium⁻²⁴⁹ with oxygen⁻¹⁸ nuclei.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Seaborgium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Seaborgium,** with the **atomic number 106,** is classified as a transuranium element. It is artificially created by** bombarding californium⁻²⁴⁹ with oxygen⁻¹⁸ nuclei**.
 
• As a synthetic element, seaborgium is solid at room temperature and belongs to the transition metal group. Its most stable isotope, seaborgium⁻²⁶⁶, has a half-life of 27.3 seconds.
 
• In 1994, the proposal to name element 106 "seaborgium" was made in tribute to Glenn T. Seaborg, the scientist credited with discovering the transuranium elements.
 
• Seaborg, an American chemist, was awarded the 1951 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for his pioneering work in the field.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Dubnium (Db)** is an artificially generated radioactive transuranium element situated in Group Vb of the periodic table, with an atomic number of 105. The discovery of dubnium, much like that of rutherfordium (element 104), has been the subject of contention between Soviet and American scientists.
 
• **Hassium (Hs)** is another artificially produced element belonging to the transuranium group, with an atomic number of 108. It was first synthesized and identified in 1984 by researchers from West Germany at the Institute for Heavy Ion Research (Gesellschaft für Schwerionenforschung [GSI]) in Darmstadt.
 
• **Copernicium** is a synthetic chemical element characterized by the symbol Cn and atomic number 112. Its known isotopes are profoundly radioactive and have exclusively been generated within laboratory settings.
